questions.question: When you give a model a tool, what does it actually receive?
options: The function's source code
A name, a description, and a JSON Schema for the parameters
A compiled binary it can execute
Only the function name
questions.explanation: The function body is invisible to the model. It decides when and how to call purely from the name, description, and schema.

questions.question: In function_to_tool, what makes a parameter required?
options: Its type is not Optional
It has no default value in the signature
It appears first in the signature
It has a description in the docstring
questions.explanation: Required means no default. Optional[int] = None is optional because of the default, not because of Optional.

questions.question: Why set additionalProperties to false?
options: It makes the schema smaller
So invented arguments like 'seat' are rejected instead of silently ignored
Anthropic requires it for every tool
It disables nested objects
questions.explanation: Without it, unknown keys pass validation and the model never learns the argument doesn't exist.

questions.question: Why does the validator explicitly reject True for an integer field?
options: JSON has no booleans
In Python, bool is a subclass of int, so isinstance(True, int) is True
Booleans are too large for integers
Models never send booleans
questions.explanation: JSON Schema treats boolean and integer as distinct types, but Python's isinstance would accept True as an int.

questions.question: The model keeps sending 'next friday' for a date. What's the cheapest effective fix?
options: Fine-tune the model
Put the format in the parameter description, e.g. 'Departure date as YYYY-MM-DD', and return a specific validation error
Remove the date parameter
Increase the temperature
questions.explanation: Descriptions are prompts. Stating the format, plus a precise error when it's wrong, fixes most argument-format problems.

questions.question: Why return all validation problems at once instead of the first one?
options: It's required by JSON Schema
So the model can fix every problem in a single retry, saving turns and tokens
It makes logs shorter
The first error is usually wrong
questions.explanation: One error per turn means one retry per error. Reporting everything lets the model correct the whole call at once.
